Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.1 Text Alternatives - 1.1.1 Non-text Content
Preconditions: Guideline 1.1  Text Alternatives: Provide text alternatives for any non-text content Success Criterion  1.1.1 Non-text Content  (Level A)
Step: Verify functional images (buttons, links) with accessibility inspector
Additional Info: axe-core (wcag111): aria-meter-name, aria-progressbar-name, image-alt, input-image-alt, object-alt, role-img-alt, svg-img-alt
Expected Result: Functional images must describe the action or destination, not just the visual image

Step: Review complex images (charts, diagrams) and look for extended descriptions
Expected Result: Complex images must have accessible long description via longdesc, aria-describedby, or adjacent text

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.2 Time-based Media - 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.2  Provide alternatives for time-based media. Success Criteria:    1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
Step: Inspect prerecorded audio-only and video-only media to verify a text transcript or audio track is provided adjacent to the player
Expected Result: Every prerecorded audio-only or video-only clip provides an accessible link or expandable section containing the full text alternative

Step: Verify that transcript includes speaker identification and relevant sounds
Expected Result: Transcript must be complete, identify who is speaking, and describe important sounds for comprehension

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.2 Time-based Media - 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.2  Provide alternatives for time-based media. Success Criteria:    1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded)
Step: Play prerecorded video content with audio and enable closed captions using keyboard and pointer controls
Expected Result: Captions are available, can be toggled on/off via accessible controls, and display all dialogue

Step: Verify caption synchronization and accuracy with audio
Expected Result: Captions must appear synchronized with audio, without significant errors, covering relevant sound effects

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.2 Time-based Media - 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.2  Provide alternatives for time-based media. Success Criteria:    1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
Step: Play videos with essential visual content and verify descriptions
Expected Result: Audio description or text alternative must exist describing important visual information

Step: Verify that alternative covers all critical visual elements for comprehension
Expected Result: Description must include actions, expressions, scene changes, and unspoken on-screen text

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.2 Time-based Media - 1.2.4 Captions (Live)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.2  Provide alternatives for time-based media. Success Criteria:    1.2.4 Captions (Live)
Step: Access live broadcasts if available
Expected Result: Live broadcasts must have real-time captioning

Step: Verify accuracy and acceptable delay of live captions
Expected Result: Captions must reflect spoken audio with reasonable accuracy and minimal delay (maximum 3-5 seconds)

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.2 Time-based Media - 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.2  Provide alternatives for time-based media. Success Criteria:    1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded)
Step: Identify prerecorded videos containing essential visual information not conveyed in audio
Expected Result: Videos must include audio description covering actions, characters, scene changes, and relevant visual elements

Step: Play video with audio description enabled and verify synchronization
Expected Result: Audio description must be inserted in natural pauses without overlapping main audio

Step: Verify that audio description covers all critical visual elements
Expected Result: Essential visual information must be fully described for blind or low vision users

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.2 Time-based Media - 1.2.6 Sign Language (Prerecorded)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.2  Provide alternatives for time-based media. Success Criteria:    1.2.6 Sign Language (Prerecorded) General Objective: To verify that pre-recorded video content with audio provides extended audio descriptions when necessary to understand the content. This test case verifies whether a pre-recorded video on the web site provides extended audio descriptions at times necessary to understand the content. Extended audio descriptions provide information about actions, characters, scenes, and on-screen information that cannot be understood from the original audio of the pre-recorded video alone. Expected Result: The pre-recorded video with audio provides extended audio descriptions at times necessary to understand the content. The extended audio descriptions can be activated and provide additional information that is not available in the original audio of the video.
Step: Identify prerecorded audio content (videos with narration or dialogue)
Expected Result: Videos must include sign language interpretation visible on screen or activatable

Step: Verify visibility and size of sign language interpreter
Expected Result: Interpreter must be clearly visible, with adequate contrast and sufficient size to distinguish signs

Step: Verify synchronization between audio and sign language
Expected Result: Sign interpretation must be synchronized with spoken audio without significant delays

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.2 Time-based Media - 1.2.7 Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.2  Provide alternatives for time-based media. Success Criteria:    1.2.7 Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
Step: Identify videos where natural pauses are insufficient for audio description
Expected Result: Video must automatically pause to allow extended audio description of complex visual information

Step: Play video with extended audio description and verify pauses
Expected Result: Video must pause when needed to describe visual elements, then continue automatically

Step: Verify user control over extended audio description
Expected Result: User must be able to enable or disable extended audio description per preference

Step: Confirm that extended description does not interfere with content comprehension
Expected Result: Pauses and descriptions must integrate naturally without causing confusion or loss of narrative context

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.2 Time-based Media - 1.2.8 Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.2  Provide alternatives for time-based media. Success Criteria:    1.2.8 Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
Step: Locate prerecorded videos and verify availability of complete text document
Expected Result: A complete text transcript must exist including dialogues, visual descriptions, and relevant sounds

Step: Review that text alternative describes complete sequence of visual events
Expected Result: Document must function as independent alternative, describing all essential visual information chronologically

Step: Verify accessibility of text alternative
Expected Result: Transcript must be in accessible format (HTML, structured document) near the original video

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.2 Time-based Media - 1.2.9 Audio-only (Live)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.2  Provide alternatives for time-based media. Success Criteria:    1.2.9 Audio-only (Live)
Step: Access live audio-only broadcast (podcast, web radio, conference)
Expected Result: An equivalent alternative must be presented synchronized with the live audio

Step: Verify delivery method of synchronized alternative
Expected Result: Alternative can be real-time transcript, synchronized text description, or updated equivalent content

Step: Verify that alternative captures essential information from live audio
Expected Result: Text content must reflect critical audio information with minimal acceptable delay

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.3 Adaptable - 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
Preconditions: Guideline 1.3  Create content that can be presented in different ways (for example simpler layout) without losing information or structure. Success Criteria:    1.3.1 Info and Relationships
Step: Verify forms with programmatically associated labels
Additional Info: axe-core (wcag131): aria-hidden-body, aria-required-children, aria-required-parent, definition-list, dlitem, list, listitem, td-headers-attr, th-has-data-cells, p-as-heading, table-fake-caption, td-has-header
Expected Result: Each input must have label with for attribute or be wrapped in label, visible to screen readers

Step: Review related field groups with fieldset and legend
Expected Result: Control groups (radio buttons, checkboxes) must be grouped with fieldset and descriptive legend

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.3 Adaptable - 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence
Preconditions: Guideline 1.3  Create content that can be presented in different ways (for example simpler layout) without losing information or structure. Success Criteria:    1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence
Step: Navigate the site using only Tab and verify reading order
Expected Result: Tab and DOM order must match the logical visual order of content

Step: Use screen reader to verify content reading order
Expected Result: Reading order must be logical and coherent, without confusing jumps caused by CSS positioning

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.3 Adaptable - 1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics
Preconditions: Guideline 1.3  Create content that can be presented in different ways (for example simpler layout) without losing information or structure. Success Criteria:    1.3.3 Sensory Characteristics
Step: Identify instructions that use only shape, color, or position
Expected Result: Instructions must include descriptive text in addition to visual references (e.g., 'green Submit button' not just 'green button')

Step: Verify that critical information does not rely solely on sensory elements
Expected Result: Errors, alerts, or process steps must be communicated with text in addition to color, icons, or sounds

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.3 Adaptable - 1.3.4 Orientation
Preconditions: Guideline 1.3  Create content that can be presented in different ways (for example simpler layout) without losing information or structure. Success Criteria:    1.3.4 Orientation
Step: Rotate the viewport between Portrait (390x844) and Landscape (812x375) orientations and inspect CSS/JS restrictions
Expected Result: Content and functionality adapt to both portrait and landscape orientations without CSS rotation locks or screen.orientation.lock() restrictions

Step: Verify that content is not locked to a single orientation
Expected Result: Application must not force specific orientation unless essential (e.g., piano app, bank check)

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.3 Adaptable - 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose
Preconditions: Guideline 1.3  Create content that can be presented in different ways (for example simpler layout) without losing information or structure. Success Criteria:    1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose
Step: Inspect form fields in source code
Expected Result: Common fields (name, email, phone) must have appropriate autocomplete attribute

Step: Test autocomplete with browser saved data
Expected Result: Fields with correct autocomplete must suggest user saved values when typing begins

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.3 Adaptable - 1.3.6 Identify Purpose
Preconditions: Guideline 1.3  Create content that can be presented in different ways (for example simpler layout) without losing information or structure. Success Criteria:    1.3.6 Identify Purpose
Step: Review complex UI components and verify programmatic purpose
Expected Result: Components must identify their purpose through ARIA attributes or HTML semantics for assistive technologies

Step: Verify icons and interactive elements with accessibility inspector
Expected Result: Buttons, links, and icons must expose their function through appropriate roles and accessible names

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.1 Use of Color
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.1 Use of Color
Step: Inspect links within blocks of text, form validation errors, charts, and status indicators to verify non-color visual cues
Expected Result: Links in text have underlines or a 3:1 contrast ratio with surrounding text plus a non-color hover/focus indicator, and statuses include icons, patterns, or text labels

Step: Test site in grayscale mode or with color blindness simulator
Expected Result: All information must remain comprehensible without relying on color to distinguish elements

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.2 Audio Control
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.2 Audio Control
Step: Load the page and observe whether any audio plays automatically for more than 3 seconds
Expected Result: Audio either does not start automatically, stops within 3 seconds, or provides a dedicated mechanism at the top of the page to pause, stop, or mute it independently of system volume

Step: Verify that audio control is keyboard accessible
Expected Result: Control must be operable without mouse, using Tab and Enter/Space

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)
Step: Verify contrast in all states (normal, hover, focus, disabled)
Expected Result: All interactive element states must meet required contrast ratios

Step: Review text over images or gradient backgrounds
Expected Result: Overlaid text must have sufficient contrast throughout or use shadows/overlays

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.4 Resize Text
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.4 Resize text
Step: Increase browser zoom and root text size up to 200% and inspect all text containers and meta viewport attributes
Expected Result: The meta viewport does not disable user scaling (no user-scalable=no or maximum-scale<2) and all text scales up to 200% without clipping, overlap, or loss of content

Step: Verify that controls and buttons remain operable when zoomed
Expected Result: Interactive elements must not be clipped or hidden when text size is increased

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.5 Images of Text
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.5 Images of Text
Step: Identify text rendered as image
Expected Result: Text must be in real HTML, not images (except logos or special cases)

Step: Inspect graphics and banners for embedded text
Expected Result: Titles, labels, and informative text must be CSS-styled HTML text, not images

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.6 Contrast (Enhanced)
Step: Measure foreground-to-background contrast ratios across normal text and large text against AAA thresholds
Expected Result: Normal text achieves a contrast ratio of at least 7:1 and large text (>=24px or >=18.66px bold) achieves at least 4.5:1

Step: Document exceptions and plan contrast improvements
Expected Result: Identify areas not meeting AAA and prioritize changes in most critical elements

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.7 Low or No Background Audio
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.7 Low or No Background Audio
Step: Play audio content and evaluate background sound presence
Expected Result: Background audio must be removable, 20dB lower than main audio, or non-existent

Step: Verify control to disable background music if present
Expected Result: User must be able to mute or reduce ambient audio without affecting main narration

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.8 Visual Presentation
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.8 Visual Presentation
Step: Verify if user can customize spacing, column width, alignment, and fonts
Expected Result: System must allow visual presentation adjustments without loss of functionality or content

Step: Test readability with OS settings (text size, high contrast)
Expected Result: Content must respect user preferences defined at system level

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.9 Images of Text (No Exception)
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.9 Images of Text (No Exception)
Step: Thoroughly review entire site for text rendered as images
Expected Result: No text in image format must exist, all must be real HTML text (no exceptions except logos)

Step: Inspect decorative elements and verify text is styled with CSS
Expected Result: Visual text effects must be achieved with CSS, not by converting text to images

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.10 Reflow
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.10 Reflow
Step: Resize window to 320px width or zoom to 400%
Expected Result: Horizontal scrolling must not be required to read content (except complex tables)

Step: Test on real mobile device with narrow viewport
Expected Result: All content must adapt fluidly without clipping or need for bidirectional scrolling

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.11 Non-text Contrast
Step: Measure contrast of UI components and focus states
Expected Result: Minimum 3:1 contrast for component borders, functional icons, and focus indicators

Step: Verify contrast of informative graphic elements (charts, status icons)
Expected Result: Visual elements conveying information must be clearly distinguishable from background

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.12 Text Spacing
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.12 Text Spacing
Step: Apply WCAG text spacing overrides (line-height: 1.5, letter-spacing: 0.12em, word-spacing: 0.16em, paragraph margin-bottom: 2em)
Expected Result: All text blocks apply the spacing overrides without being blocked by inline !important styles and without horizontal scroll or clipped text

Step: Verify that buttons and controls do not break with modified spacing
Expected Result: Interactive elements must maintain functionality and readability with custom spacing

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 1.4 Distinguishable - 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus
Preconditions: Guideline 1.4  Make it easier for users to see and hear content including separating foreground from background. Success Criteria:    1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus
Step: Activate tooltips and popup content with hover and keyboard
Expected Result: Additional content must be keyboard accessible, remain visible, and be dismissible without moving pointer

Step: Verify that popup content does not disappear when moving pointer over it
Expected Result: User must be able to move cursor over tooltip to read or interact without it disappearing

Step: Verify accessible dismiss mechanism (ESC or close button)
Expected Result: Popup content must be dismissible without moving pointer from the trigger that activated it

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.1 Keyboard Accessible - 2.1.1 Keyboard
Preconditions: Guideline 2.1  All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, except where the underlying function requires input that depends on the path of the user's movement and not just the endpoints. Success Criteria: 2.1.1 Keyboard
Step: Test complex components (accordions, tabs, calendars)
Expected Result: Custom widgets must respond to appropriate keys (arrows, Home, End, Escape)

Step: Verify all mouse actions have keyboard equivalent
Expected Result: Drag and drop, hover menus, touch gestures must have keyboard-operable alternatives

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.1 Keyboard Accessible - 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap
Preconditions: Guideline 2.1  All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, except where the underlying function requires input that depends on the path of the user's movement and not just the endpoints. Success Criteria: 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap
Step: Navigate the entire page/component using only Tab and Shift+Tab
Expected Result: Focus must move through all interactive elements and exit freely without being trapped

Step: Test modals, dialogs, and overlays with keyboard navigation
Expected Result: Focus must move freely within the component and it must be closable via Esc or a keyboard-accessible close control

Step: If content requires non-standard keys to exit focus, verify users are informed
Expected Result: Instructions for un-trapping focus must be visibly provided

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.1 Keyboard Accessible - 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception)
Preconditions: Guideline 2.1  Make all functionality available from a keyboard. Success Criteria:    2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception)
Step: Navigate and operate every interactive component and custom widget using only the keyboard without exception
Expected Result: All page functionality is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes

Step: Document functions requiring specific pointer path
Expected Result: If function requires specific path (signature, drawing), keyboard alternative or alternative method must exist

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.1 Keyboard Accessible - 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts
Preconditions: Guideline 2.1  All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, except where the underlying function requires input that depends on the path of the user's movement and not just the endpoints. Success Criteria: 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcut
Step: Identify single-key shortcuts (letter, number, or punctuation) implemented in the interface
Expected Result: Each shortcut must be disableable, remappable, or active only while its component has focus

Step: Verify shortcuts do not interfere with screen readers or assistive tools
Expected Result: Key combinations must avoid conflicts with assistive technology commands

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.2 Enough Time - 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable
Preconditions: Guideline 2.2  Give users enough time to read and use content. Success Criteria:    2.2.1 Timing Adjustable
Step: Inspect session timeouts, automatic redirects, and meta http-equiv refresh tags on the page
Expected Result: No timed meta refresh is present, and any session time limit can be turned off, adjusted to at least 10x the default, or extended with at least 20 seconds notice

Step: Verify prior warning before time expires
Expected Result: System must alert with sufficient advance notice and allow simple extension (e.g., press button)

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.2 Enough Time - 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide
Preconditions: Guideline 2.2  Give users enough time to read and use content. Success Criteria:    2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide
Step: Inspect carousels, auto-updating tickers, animations, and blinking/scrolling content lasting more than 5 seconds
Expected Result: No <blink> or <marquee> elements exist, and any moving, blinking, or auto-updating content has a mechanism to pause, stop, or hide it

Step: Verify pause control is visible and keyboard operable
Expected Result: Pause/play buttons must be clearly visible and accessible without mouse

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.2 Enough Time - 2.2.3 No Timing
Preconditions: Guideline 2.2  Give users enough time to read and use content. Success Criteria:    2.2.3 No Timing
Step: Verify that all functionality and content can be used without any time limits
Expected Result: Tasks must be completable without time restrictions or interruptions

Step: Document exceptions where time is a real-time requirement
Expected Result: Only live essential events (e.g. real-time auctions) may be exempt; all others must have no timing

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.2 Enough Time - 2.2.4 Interruptions
Preconditions: Guideline 2.2  Give users enough time to read and use content. Success Criteria:    2.2.4 Interruptions
Step: Trigger non-emergency notifications, promotional banners, or automatic page refreshes during a user task
Expected Result: Interruptions and non-essential updates can be postponed or suppressed by the user without losing current task progress

Step: Verify notification preferences settings
Expected Result: System must offer controls to manage frequency and type of interruptions

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.2 Enough Time - 2.2.5 Re-authenticating
Preconditions: Guideline 2.2  Give users enough time to read and use content. Success Criteria:    2.2.5 Re-authenticating
Step: Let the session expire mid-task and log in again
Expected Result: After re-authenticating, the user must continue the activity without losing previously entered data

Step: Test with long forms and verify data recovery
Expected Result: In-progress information must be auto-saved or recoverable after relogin

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.2 Enough Time - 2.2.6 Timeouts
Preconditions: Guideline 2.2  Give users enough time to read and use content. Success Criteria:    2.2.6 Timeouts
Step: Verify users are warned about session inactivity timeout
Expected Result: A warning must be presented in time for the user to react (at least 20 seconds) via an accessible notification

Step: Verify user can save work before timeout
Expected Result: Warning must include a clear option to save progress or extend the session

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.3 Seizures and Physical Reactions - 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold
Preconditions: Guideline 2.3  Do not design content in a way that is known to cause seizures or physical reactions. Success Criteria:    2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold
Step: Review site animations and transitions
Expected Result: No content should flash more than 3 times per second

Step: Use PEAT (Photosensitive Epilepsy Analysis Tool) if available
Expected Result: Analyze multimedia content to identify flashes that could cause seizures

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.3 Seizures and Physical Reactions - 2.3.2 Three Flashes
Preconditions: Guideline 2.3  Do not design content in a way that is known to cause seizures or physical reactions. Success Criteria:    2.3.2 Three Flashes
Step: Thoroughly analyze animations, videos, and dynamic content
Expected Result: No flash exceeding safe limits must exist, without exceptions

Step: Review embedded third-party content (ads, external videos)
Expected Result: External content must not contain dangerous flashes or must be disableable

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.3 Seizures and Physical Reactions - 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions
Preconditions: Guideline 2.3  Do not design content in a way that is known to cause seizures or physical reactions. Success Criteria:    2.3.3 Animation from Interactions
Step: Verify motion animations triggered by scroll or interaction
Expected Result: User must be able to disable non-essential motion animations

Step: Verify respect for system prefers-reduced-motion preference
Expected Result: Site must detect and respect OS setting to reduce motion

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.1 Bypass Blocks
Step: Press Tab from the address bar on page load to check for a skip-to-main-content link and verify focus movement
Expected Result: A skip link becomes visible on focus and activating it moves keyboard focus directly to the main content container

Step: Verify ARIA landmarks (main, nav, complementary, contentinfo)
Expected Result: Structure must use landmark roles to enable quick navigation with screen readers

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.2 Page Titled
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.2 Page Titled
Step: Inspect the document <title> element in the DOM and observe title updates across SPA route changes
Expected Result: Every page and view has a non-empty, descriptive <title> element that clearly identifies the current screen or step

Step: Verify title follows consistent format (content - section - site name)
Expected Result: Titles must follow predictable pattern facilitating identification in tabs and history

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.3 Focus Order
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.3 Focus Order
Step: Navigate with Tab in order and verify visual logic
Expected Result: Focus order must follow logical sequence left to right, top to bottom

Step: Identify elements with positive tabindex and evaluate necessity
Expected Result: Avoid tabindex greater than 0, order must be controlled through logical DOM structure

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)
Step: Inspect all <a href>, area[href], and role=link elements to verify their accessible name and destination context
Expected Result: Every link has a non-empty accessible name that describes its purpose alone or together with its enclosing sentence/list item, and target=_blank links warn of new window

Step: Use screen reader to list all links
Expected Result: Links must be understandable when presented out of context in link list

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.5 Multiple Ways
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.5 Multiple Ways
Step: Try to locate an internal page in different ways
Expected Result: Navigation menu, internal search, sitemap, or breadcrumbs must exist

Step: Verify at least two navigation methods are available
Expected Result: User must be able to choose between different strategies to locate content

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.6 Headings and Labels
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.6 Headings and Labels
Step: Verify page headings are descriptive and reflect the content structure
Expected Result: Each heading must clearly describe the topic or purpose of its section

Step: Use screen reader to navigate by headings
Expected Result: Heading structure must allow quick understanding of content organization

Step: Check labels of form fields and interactive controls
Expected Result: All labels must be descriptive and clearly identify the control purpose

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.7 Focus Visible
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.7 Focus Visible
Step: Navigate with Tab and observe focus indicator
Expected Result: Interactive elements must show clear contrasted visual indicator when focused

Step: Verify outline is not disabled without visual replacement
Expected Result: If default outline is removed, equally visible alternative indicator must exist

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.8 Location
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.8 Location
Step: Navigate through different site sections and verify location indicators
Expected Result: Breadcrumbs, section titles, or indicators showing user location must exist

Step: Review that breadcrumbs are accessible and reflect correct hierarchy
Expected Result: Breadcrumbs must be keyboard navigable and structured with ordered list

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only)
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.9 Link Purpose (Link Only)
Step: Inspect all links on the page in isolation (ignoring surrounding paragraph text) and compare links sharing the same accessible name
Expected Result: Each link accessible name uniquely and clearly describes its destination on its own, and links with identical names point to the same resource

Step: Identify generic links ('more info', 'read more') and improve them
Expected Result: Ambiguous links must include additional context via aria-label or aria-describedby

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.10 Section Headings
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.10 Section Headings
Step: Review content structure and heading usage
Expected Result: Content must be organized with descriptive headings dividing information into logical sections

Step: Verify no long text blocks exist without intermediate headings
Expected Result: Extensive content must be subdivided with headings facilitating scanning and navigation

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
Step: Navigate with keyboard and verify focus visibility on elements near edges
Expected Result: At least part of focus indicator must remain visible, not completely hidden by other elements

Step: Test navigation in areas with sticky headers or floating elements
Expected Result: Sticky bars must not completely cover the focused element

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.12 Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
Step: Verify focus is completely visible in all situations
Expected Result: Focus indicator must be completely visible without any obstruction by other elements

Step: Implement auto-scroll when element receives focus outside viewport
Expected Result: Content must auto-adjust to fully show the focused element

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.4 Navigable - 2.4.13 Focus Appearance
Preconditions: Guideline 2.4  Provide ways to help users navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Success Criteria:    2.4.13 Focus Appearance
Step: Measure focus indicator area and contrast with specialized tools
Expected Result: Indicator must have sufficient minimum area and high contrast for maximum visibility

Step: Calculate that indicator has minimum 2 CSS pixels perimeter or equivalent area
Expected Result: Indicator thickness and area must meet specific WCAG 2.2 requirements

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.5 Input Modalities - 2.5.1 Pointer Gestures
Preconditions: Guideline 2.5  Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs beyond keyboard. Success Criteria:    2.5.1 Pointer Gestures
Step: Identify functions activated by complex gestures (swipe, pinch)
Expected Result: Functions must have alternative with simple single-point gestures (tap, click)

Step: Verify carousels, maps, and swipeable components
Expected Result: Alternative buttons or controls must exist for users with motor limitations

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.5 Input Modalities - 2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation
Preconditions: Guideline 2.5  Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs beyond keyboard. Success Criteria:    2.5.2 Pointer Cancellation
Step: Test activation of interactive elements
Expected Result: Function must not execute on mousedown/touchstart, must allow cancellation by releasing outside target

Step: Verify accidental clicks can be cancelled by dragging outside
Expected Result: User must be able to undo accidental activation by moving pointer before release

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.5 Input Modalities - 2.5.3 Label in Name
Preconditions: Guideline 2.5  Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs beyond keyboard. Success Criteria:    2.5.3 Label in Name
Step: Compare the visible text label of every button, link, and form control against its computed accessible name (aria-label / aria-labelledby)
Expected Result: For every control with a visible text label, the accessible name contains the exact visible text string (preferably at the beginning)

Step: Verify voice commands can activate controls using visible text
Expected Result: Voice control users must be able to say visible text to activate element

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.5 Input Modalities - 2.5.4 Motion Actuation
Preconditions: Guideline 2.5  Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs beyond keyboard. Success Criteria:    2.5.4 Motion Actuation
Step: Identify functions using accelerometer or gyroscope
Expected Result: Functions activated by device motion must have standard UI alternative

Step: Verify setting to disable motion actuation
Expected Result: User must be able to disable motion responses to avoid accidental activations

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.5 Input Modalities - 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced)
Preconditions: Guideline 2.5  Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs beyond keyboard. Success Criteria:    2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced)
Step: Measure dimensions of all pointer targets (buttons, links, controls)
Expected Result: All targets must be at least 44x44 CSS pixels, except inline links within sentences or user-agent controlled elements

Step: Verify exceptions: inline text links, equivalent controls, or legal/presentation requirements
Expected Result: If a target is smaller than 44x44, an equivalent alternative control with adequate size must exist

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.5 Input Modalities - 2.5.6 Concurrent Input Mechanisms
Preconditions: Guideline 2.5  Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs beyond keyboard. Success Criteria:    2.5.6 Concurrent Input Mechanisms
Step: Test site with multiple simultaneous input devices (keyboard + mouse + touch)
Expected Result: Site must support simultaneous use of different input mechanisms without restrictions

Step: Verify switching input method does not cause loss of functionality
Expected Result: User must be able to freely switch between keyboard, mouse, and touch without issues

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.5 Input Modalities - 2.5.7 Dragging Movements
Preconditions: Guideline 2.5  Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs beyond keyboard. Success Criteria:    2.5.7 Dragging Movements
Step: Identify drag and drop functions
Expected Result: Drag and drop functions must have alternative with simple clicks or taps

Step: Test keyboard alternatives for reordering elements
Expected Result: Reorderable lists must be manipulable with keyboard (arrows + Space/Enter)

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 2.5 Input Modalities - 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)
Preconditions: Guideline 2.5  Make it easier for users to operate functionality through various inputs beyond keyboard. Success Criteria:    2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum)
Step: Measure dimensions of touch controls (buttons, links)
Expected Result: Touch targets must have minimum 24x24 CSS pixels or equivalent spacing

Step: Verify spacing between adjacent touch targets
Expected Result: If targets are smaller than 24px, sufficient surrounding space must exist to avoid errors

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.1 Readable - 3.1.1 Language of Page
Preconditions: Guideline 3.1  Make text content readable and understandable. Success Criteria:    3.1.1 Language of Page
Step: Inspect the <html> root element for the lang attribute (and xml:lang if present) in the DOM
Expected Result: The <html> element has a non-empty, valid BCP-47 lang attribute matching the primary language of the document (and xml:lang matches if present)

Step: Verify correct pronunciation with screen reader
Expected Result: Reader must use voice and pronunciation rules appropriate to declared language

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.1 Readable - 3.1.2 Language of Parts
Preconditions: Guideline 3.1  Make text content readable and understandable. Success Criteria:    3.1.2 Language of Parts
Step: Locate passages, phrases, or terms written in a language different from the page primary language and inspect their [lang] attribute
Expected Result: Every foreign-language passage or phrase (excluding proper names and technical terms) has a valid BCP-47 lang attribute on its container

Step: Test screen reader reading of quotes or terms in another language
Expected Result: Language changes must be recognized and pronounced correctly

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.1 Readable - 3.1.3 Unusual Words
Preconditions: Guideline 3.1  Make text content readable and understandable. Success Criteria:    3.1.3 Unusual Words
Step: Identify jargon, technical terms, or unusual words in content
Expected Result: Glossary, inline definitions, or mechanism to explain uncommon terms must exist

Step: Verify accessibility of definitions through links or dfn/abbr elements
Expected Result: Specialized terms must link to accessible explanations

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.1 Readable - 3.1.4 Abbreviations
Preconditions: Guideline 3.1  Make text content readable and understandable. Success Criteria:    3.1.4 Abbreviations
Step: Locate abbreviations and acronyms in content
Expected Result: First instance of abbreviations must include full expansion or link to definition

Step: Implement abbr element with title attribute where appropriate
Expected Result: Abbreviations must be semantically marked for assistive technologies

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.1 Readable - 3.1.5 Reading Level
Preconditions: Guideline 3.1  Make text content readable and understandable. Success Criteria:    3.1.5 Reading Level
Step: Evaluate text complexity and required reading level
Expected Result: Complex content must have simplified version or summary for lower secondary education level

Step: Use readability analysis tools (Flesch-Kincaid, INFLESZ)
Expected Result: Measure readability indices and provide alternatives for technical or complex content

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.1 Readable - 3.1.6 Pronunciation
Preconditions: Guideline 3.1  Make text content readable and understandable. Success Criteria:    3.1.6 Pronunciation
Step: Identify words where pronunciation is critical for comprehension
Expected Result: Mechanism to indicate pronunciation must exist (IPA, audio, phonetic text)

Step: Verify homographs and ambiguous terms with pronunciation guides
Expected Result: Words with multiple pronunciations must be clarified when context is insufficient

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.2 Predictable - 3.2.1 On Focus
Preconditions: Guideline 3.2  Make Web pages appear and operate in predictable ways. Success Criteria:    3.2.1 On Focus
Step: Navigate with Tab through interactive elements
Expected Result: No element should cause context change (navigation, submission) just by receiving focus

Step: Verify form fields do not submit when focused
Expected Result: Focus must be independent of activation, changes must only occur with explicit action

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.2 Predictable - 3.2.2 On Input
Preconditions: Guideline 3.2  Make Web pages appear and operate in predictable ways. Success Criteria:    3.2.2 On Input
Step: Interact with forms and controls without activating submit button
Expected Result: Field changes must not cause context change without prior warning or confirmation

Step: Test selects and radios that may cause automatic navigation
Expected Result: If change causes action, prior warning or confirmation button must be required

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.2 Predictable - 3.2.3 Consistent Navigation
Preconditions: Guideline 3.2  Make Web pages appear and operate in predictable ways. Success Criteria:    3.2.3 Consistent Navigation
Step: Compare menus and navigation across different pages
Expected Result: Repeated navigation elements must appear in same order across all pages

Step: Document location of global elements (search, login, main menu)
Expected Result: Common components must maintain consistent position and order throughout site

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.2 Predictable - 3.2.4 Consistent Identification
Preconditions: Guideline 3.2  Make Web pages appear and operate in predictable ways. Success Criteria:    3.2.4 Consistent Identification
Step: Identify components with same function across different pages
Expected Result: Equivalent components must use same labels, icons, and accessible names

Step: Verify consistency of icons and symbols throughout site
Expected Result: Same icon must represent same function, avoid different symbols for identical actions

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.2 Predictable - 3.2.5 Change on Request
Preconditions: Guideline 3.2  Make Web pages appear and operate in predictable ways. Success Criteria:    3.2.5 Change on Request
Step: Verify significant changes require explicit user action
Expected Result: Context changes, submissions, or navigation must not occur without explicit confirmation

Step: Identify and fix automatic submissions or unexpected redirects
Expected Result: User must initiate all important changes through clear buttons or links

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.2 Predictable - 3.2.6 Consistent Help
Preconditions: Guideline 3.2 Predictable: Make Web pages appear and operate in predictable ways. Success Criteria: 3.2.6 Consistent Help (A) - If a Web page contains help mechanisms, and those mechanisms are repeated on multiple Web pages within a set of Web pages, they occur in the same relative order to other page content, unless a change is initiated by the user.
Step: Search for help mechanisms in different sections
Expected Result: Help options must appear in consistent location throughout site

Step: Verify quick access to contact, FAQ, chat, or documentation
Expected Result: Help must be available predictably in fixed location

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.3 Input Assistance - 3.3.1 Error Identification
Preconditions: Guideline 3.3  Help users avoid and correct mistakes. Success Criteria:    3.3.1 Error Identification
Step: Submit form with intentional errors
Expected Result: Errors must be clearly identified in text, visually marked, and announced to screen readers

Step: Verify error messages use aria-describedby or aria-invalid
Expected Result: Errors must be programmatically associated with affected fields for assistive technologies

Step: Verify focus moves to first error or error summary
Expected Result: After validation, user must be clearly directed to found problems

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.3 Input Assistance - 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
Preconditions: Guideline 3.3  Help users avoid and correct mistakes. Success Criteria:    3.3.2 Labels or Instructions
Step: Inspect all form controls (inputs, selects, textareas, custom ARIA inputs) for visible labels, required indicators, and format instructions
Expected Result: Every data entry control has a persistent visible label programmatically linked to it, and required state or input format constraints are clearly stated before the field

Step: Verify fields with specific formats (date, phone, zip code)
Expected Result: Fields with format requirements must include examples or input masks

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.3 Input Assistance - 3.3.3 Error Suggestion
Preconditions: Guideline 3.3  Help users avoid and correct mistakes. Success Criteria:    3.3.3 Error Suggestion
Step: Trigger validation errors in forms
Expected Result: Error messages must suggest how to fix the specific problem

Step: Evaluate message quality: must be specific and solution-oriented
Expected Result: Errors must explain what is wrong and how to fix it, not just indicate there is an error

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.3 Input Assistance - 3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
Preconditions: Guideline 3.3  Help users avoid and correct mistakes. Success Criteria:    3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
Step: Complete financial or legal transactions if they exist
Expected Result: Must allow reviewing, confirming, and correcting information before final submission

Step: Verify confirmation page with option to edit before final submission
Expected Result: Critical data must be shown in summary with ability to go back and modify

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.3 Input Assistance - 3.3.5 Help
Preconditions: Guideline 3.3  Help users avoid and correct mistakes. Success Criteria:    3.3.5 Help
Step: Search for contextual help in forms and complex tasks
Expected Result: Available help must exist to complete tasks, visible or easily accessible

Step: Verify tooltips, help links, or info icons next to complex fields
Expected Result: Help must be available in context where needed, not only on separate page

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.3 Input Assistance - 3.3.6 Error Prevention (All)
Preconditions: Guideline 3.3  Help users avoid and correct mistakes. Success Criteria:    3.3.6 Error Prevention (All)
Step: Identify forms that modify, delete, or compromise user data
Expected Result: Reversible mechanism (undo), verification (review before submit), or explicit confirmation must exist

Step: Test form submission with critical information
Expected Result: System must present review screen where user can verify and correct before confirming

Step: Verify availability of option to revert completed actions
Expected Result: Destructive actions must allow undo or have grace period before permanent execution

Step: Verify explicit confirmations for irreversible actions
Expected Result: Deletions, transfers, or permanent changes must require clear and specific additional confirmation

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.3 Input Assistance - 3.3.7 Redundant Entry
Preconditions: Guideline 3.3  Help users avoid and correct mistakes. Success Criteria:    3.3.7 Redundant Entry
Step: Complete multi-step forms
Expected Result: Previously provided information must auto-complete or be selectable, not re-entered

Step: Verify data from previous steps is pre-filled in later steps
Expected Result: User must not re-type name, address, or other already entered data

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.3 Input Assistance - 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
Preconditions: Guideline 3.3  Help users avoid and correct mistakes. Success Criteria:    3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
Step: Test login and authentication process
Expected Result: Must offer accessible alternatives to visual CAPTCHA or cognitive tests (email, SMS, biometrics)

Step: Verify availability of magic link or OTP code authentication
Expected Result: Alternative methods must be equally secure without requiring visual recognition

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 3.3 Input Assistance - 3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
Preconditions: Guideline 3.3  Help users avoid and correct mistakes. Success Criteria:    3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
Step: Test authentication flows to confirm no cognitive function test is required at any step
Expected Result: Login must not depend on memorization, transcription, or puzzle solving unless an accessible alternative or assistance is provided

Step: Verify password managers and copy-paste are fully supported in credential fields
Expected Result: Users must be able to paste credentials or use password manager autofill/biometrics without restrictions

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 4.1 Compatible - 4.1.1 Parsing (Obsolete and removed)
Preconditions: Guideline 4.1  Maximize compatibility with current and future user agents, including assistive technologies. Success Criteria:    4.1.1 Parsing
Step: Check the DOM for duplicate id attributes across active elements, labels, and ARIA IDREF targets
Expected Result: All id attribute values in the document and open shadow roots are unique so label[for], aria-labelledby, and aria-describedby references never collide

Step: Review dynamically generated code with browser inspector
Expected Result: JavaScript generating content must produce valid and well-formed HTML

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 4.1 Compatible - 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
Preconditions: Guideline 4.1  Maximize compatibility with current and future user agents, including assistive technologies. Success Criteria:    4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
Step: Test custom widgets with screen reader
Additional Info: axe-core (wcag412): area-alt, aria-allowed-attr, aria-braille-equivalent, aria-command-name, aria-conditional-attr, aria-deprecated-role, aria-hidden-body, aria-hidden-focus, aria-input-field-name, aria-prohibited-attr, aria-required-attr, aria-roles, aria-tab-name, aria-toggle-field-name, aria-tooltip-name, aria-valid-attr-value, aria-valid-attr, button-name, duplicate-id-aria, frame-title-unique, frame-title, input-button-name, input-image-alt, label, link-name, nested-interactive, select-name, summary-name, aria-roledescription
Expected Result: Components must announce correctly with appropriate ARIA role, state, and properties

Step: Verify state changes are reflected in ARIA attributes
Expected Result: Dynamic states (expanded, selected, pressed) must be updated programmatically

Title: TC - [A11Y] - 4.1 Compatible - 4.1.3 Status Messages
Preconditions: Guideline 4.1  Maximize compatibility with current and future user agents, including assistive technologies. Success Criteria:    4.1.3 Status Messages
Step: Trigger dynamic messages (confirmation, error, loading)
Expected Result: Messages must be announced in screen readers using appropriate ARIA live regions

Step: Verify correct usage of role=alert, aria-live=polite/assertive
Expected Result: Critical messages use assertive, informational use polite, without moving focus

Step: Test with screen reader that announcements interrupt or wait appropriately
Expected Result: Live regions must be configured by message urgency without causing excessive interruptions
